ORDINANCE 91 - 1 AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND ORDINANCE 88-4 OF THE TOWN OF CLERMONT, GEORGIA, BUILDING PERMIT REQUIREMENTS; TO IMPOSE WATER CONSERVATION RESTRICTIONS; TO PROVIDE DEFINITIONS; TO PROVIDE FOR EXEMPTIONS; TO PROVIDE PENALTIES; TO PROVIDE FOR RELATED MATTERS; TO REPEAL CONFLICTING ORDINANCES ; TQ PROVIDE FOR SEVERABILITY; TO PROVIDE FOR CODIFICATION; TO PROVIDE FOR AN EFFECTIVE DATE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES. BE IT ORDAINED BY THE TOWN COUNCIL OF CLERMONT, GEORGIA AS FOLLOWS :

The Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia finds that an adequate supply of clean drinking water is a precious and essential resource upon which life depends; that the demand for clean watter supplies continues to increase despite the limitations of availability and affordability of such é supplies; and that there is technology available to improve the efficiency of plumbing products.

The Council desires to amend the Building Permit Procedure, as adopted by Ordinance 88-4 on October 25, 1988, so as to:

- (a) Promote greater efficiency in residential and commercial water use and preserve the natural resources of this State;

- (b) Reduce consumer water and energy costs by reducing indoor water use, reducing the need for new water supplies and treatment facilities, lowering operation and maintenance

costs for water utilities, and reducing the amount of energy used to heat, treat, and transport water; and

- (c) Generate consumer awareness of the need to save water and of the savings that can result from the use of efficient plumbing products.

The following is incorporated as a part of the Building Permit Procedure, Ordinance 88-4, of the Town of Clermont, Georgia To Wit:
1:
- (a) "Commercial" means any type of building other than residential.

- (b) "Construction" means the erection of a new building or the alteration of an existing building in connection with its repair or renovation or in connection with making an addition to an existing building and shall include the replacement of a malfunctioning, unserviceable, or obsolete faucet, showerhead, toilet, or urinal in an existing building.

- (c) "Residential" means any building or unit of a building intended for occupancy as a dwelling but shall not include a hotel-or motel.
3:
On or after July 1, 1992, there shall not be initiated within the Town of Clermont the construction of any commercial building of any type which does not meet the requirements of subparagraphs (1) through (5) of SECTION II of this Ordinance.

SECTION IV. EFFECTIVE DATES, The requirements of SECTION II of this Ordinance shall apply to any residential construction initiated after July

1, 1991 and to any commercial construction initiated after July 1, 1992, which involves the repair or renovation of or addition to any existing building when such repair or renovation of or addition to such existing building includes replacement of toilets or showers or both.
4:
- (a) New construction and the repair or renovation of an existing building shall be exempt from the requirements of SECTIONS II, III, and IV of this Ordinance when:

| (1) The repair or renovation of the existing building does not include the replacement of the plumbing or sewage system servicing toilets, faucets or showerheads within such existing buildings; or

- (2) When such plumbing or sewage system within such existing building, because of its capacity, design, or installation would not function properly if the toilets, faucets or showerheads required by this Ordinance were installed; or

- (3) Such system is a well or gravity flow from a spring and is owned privately by an individual for use in any such individual’s personal residence; or

- (4) Units to be installed are:

(A) Specifically designed for use by the

handicapped;

(B) Specifically designed to withstand unusual abuse or installation ina penal institution; or

(C) Toilets for juveniles.

- (b) The owner, or his agent, of a building undergoing new construction or repair or renovation who is entitled to an exemption as specified in subparagraph (a) (2), (3) oF (4) of this SECTION shall obtain the exemption by applying at the office of the City Clerk for the Town of Clermont. A fee of $25.00 shall be charged for the inspection and issuance of such exemption.
5:
- (a) This Ordinance shall be enforced by the office of the building inspector of the Town of Clermont. Citations for violations may be issued by the Town Council of the Town of Clermont.

- (b) Any person, corporation, partnership or other entity violating this Ordinance shall be tried before the Magistrate Court of Hall County, Georgia. Upon conviction, a violation of this Ordinance shall be punished by fine or imprisonment as conferred in the Charter for the Town of Clermont, (Acts 1913, p 674, 676 and 677).

- (c) Where a violation of this Ordinance exists, the Mayor and Town Council for the Town of Clermont may, in addition to other remedies, notify all public utilities and

city service departments (including but not limited to, the City of Gainesville Water Department) of such violation and request that service be withheld therefore until such time the violation existing under the provisions of this
7:
It is the intent of this Ordinance to provide greater efficiency in residential and commercial water use and to preserve natural resources as outlined by the City of Gainesville Ordinance No. 91- 02 since the City of Gainesville Water Department services the majority of residences within the town limits of Clermont.

SECTION VIII. REPEAL OF CONFLICTING ORDINANCES. All Ordinances and/or parts of Ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby repealed.
8:
If any paragraph, sub-paragraph, sentence, clause, phrase or any portion of this Ordinance shall be declared invalid or unconstitutional by any court of competent jurisdiction or if the provisions of any part of this Ordinance as applied to any particular situation or set of circumstances shall be declared invalid or unconstitutional, such invalidity shall not be construed to affect or impair the remaining portions unless it clearly appears that such

other parts are wholly and necessarily dependent upon the part held to be invalid or unconstitutional.

SECTION X. This Ordinance is enacted as an amendment to Ordinance 88-4 of the Code of Ordinances of the Town of Clermont,

Georgia.
9:
This Ordinance shall become effective on June 30, 1991.
